blocks.text:
Complex Listening & Inference
เป้าหมาย: ติดตามการแก้ไขคำพูดและแยกความหมายชัดแจ้งจากข้ออนุมาน

Use the language of complex listening & inference to complete the unit's practical or interpretive task.
Identify and relay the essential information in the two readings without adding unsupported facts.
Respond to the two listening scripts with appropriate clarification and source-sensitive wording.

Reading A
In a fictional planning discussion, the coordinator says, 'We can probably open on Friday—assuming the inspection is finished.' A colleague later reports, 'Friday's opening is confirmed.' The summary loses both probability and condition. Another speaker says, 'I wouldn't call the schedule comfortable,' which suggests concern without directly announcing failure. Listeners need to track hedges, corrections and what each speaker is responding to. Intonation may help, but a single pause or stressed word cannot establish a person's private intention. A careful account separates explicit commitments from reasonable inferences and checks uncertainty when the next action depends on it.

Read for purpose, then locate the people, events, conditions and limits. Map claim, supporting evidence, alternative explanation and limitation. Compare sources on the same question. Build a proportionate conclusion and address a fair counterargument. Explain why your evidence supports a claim rather than merely repeating it.

Reading B
Meeting note: Opening target—Friday. Inspection—pending. Equipment delivery—Thursday, provisionally. Staffing—confirmed for Friday afternoon only. No decision has been recorded about opening earlier or staying late.

Compare the two inputs: what is shared, what is additional, and what is not known? Use only details actually supplied. All characters, organisations, figures and events in these inputs are fictional classroom materials.

หน้าที่: รักษาทั้งความน่าจะเป็นและข้อแม้
Model: We can probably open, assuming inspection is complete.
Try: change one detail while preserving the function. Check the result against the source.

understatement
หน้าที่: ถ้อยคำอ่อนที่สื่อข้อกังวล
Model: I wouldn't call it comfortable.
Try: change one detail while preserving the function. Check the result against the source.

not … but …
หน้าที่: แยกข้อเสนอจากความเข้าใจผิด
Model: I am not saying cancel; I am saying prepare a backup.
Try: change one detail while preserving the function. Check the result against the source.

Guided practice: cover the word bank, reconstruct five target expressions, and explain their meaning in these particular contexts. Then use two in a new example. The same word may have a different sense elsewhere.

Listening script A — authored script; recorded audio and human audio QC are pending. Reading the transcript is text-based preparation, not evidence of independent listening ability.

A: We can probably open on Friday, assuming inspection is complete.
B: Is Friday confirmed, then?
A: Not yet. It is our target.
B: I'll note it as conditional and check again after inspection.
A: Good. The afternoon staff are confirmed.

Listening script B
The schedule is, well, possible, but I wouldn't call it comfortable. If the delivery slips, we have very little room to recover. I am not saying we must cancel; I am saying we need a backup and a clear decision point.

First pass: identify purpose and main message. Second pass: note essential details and any corrections. Check against the script only after the listening attempt when approved audio becomes available. For now, practise with a teacher or partner reading the script.

Pronunciation and prosody
Use prominence to distinguish your position from a reported view. Pause at changes of argument. Signal concession and contrast with phrasing, without relying on exaggerated stress to make weak evidence sound stronger.

Interaction rehearsal: take both roles. Ask one clarification question, answer it using the source, and check that the other person has understood. Do not equate quietness, accent or hesitation with lack of ability.

Unit transfer task
ติดตามการแก้ไขคำพูดและแยกความหมายชัดแจ้งจากข้ออนุมาน

Prepare a 180–240-word response and a 120–180-second spoken response using the unit inputs. Develop sustained positions, evaluate competing practical options and relay complex information with clear qualification.

Planning sequence
1. Identify audience and purpose.
2. Select source details that the audience needs.
3. Mark any uncertainty, unconfirmed arrangement or missing information.
4. Choose two language features from Lesson 2.
5. Produce the response, then check meaning before surface accuracy.

Mediation: explain the essential information to a Thai-speaking classmate who has not read the sources. Preserve dates, quantities, conditions, agency and uncertainty. Say what cannot be concluded.

Online interaction: respond to a request for clarification, then add a follow-up checking question. Acknowledge corrections and revise your message where needed.

Quick review
probably / assuming: We can probably open, assuming inspection is complete.
understatement: I wouldn't call it comfortable.
not … but …: I am not saying cancel; I am saying prepare a backup.
แยกข้ออ้าง เหตุผล ตัวอย่าง และหลักฐาน ใช้ถ้อยคำที่มีน้ำหนักพอดีกับข้อมูล โต้แย้งประเด็นจริงของอีกฝ่ายและยอมรับข้อจำกัด

Self-check: Did I meet the purpose? Which source supports each factual detail? Did I make a suggestion sound confirmed? Can the other person act or understand appropriately? Which error should I revisit tomorrow?

inputs.label: Reading A
inputs.text: In a fictional planning discussion, the coordinator says, 'We can probably open on Friday—assuming the inspection is finished.' A colleague later reports, 'Friday's opening is confirmed.' The summary loses both probability and condition. Another speaker says, 'I wouldn't call the schedule comfortable,' which suggests concern without directly announcing failure. Listeners need to track hedges, corrections and what each speaker is responding to. Intonation may help, but a single pause or stressed word cannot establish a person's private intention. A careful account separates explicit commitments from reasonable inferences and checks uncertainty when the next action depends on it.

inputs.label: Reading B
inputs.text: Meeting note: Opening target—Friday. Inspection—pending. Equipment delivery—Thursday, provisionally. Staffing—confirmed for Friday afternoon only. No decision has been recorded about opening earlier or staying late.

inputs.label: Listening script A
inputs.text:
A: We can probably open on Friday, assuming inspection is complete.
B: Is Friday confirmed, then?
A: Not yet. It is our target.
B: I'll note it as conditional and check again after inspection.
A: Good. The afternoon staff are confirmed.

inputs.label: Listening script B
inputs.text: The schedule is, well, possible, but I wouldn't call it comfortable. If the delivery slips, we have very little room to recover. I am not saying we must cancel; I am saying we need a backup and a clear decision point.

pronunciation: Use prominence to distinguish your position from a reported view. Pause at changes of argument. Signal concession and contrast with phrasing, without relying on exaggerated stress to make weak evidence sound stronger.

rubric.descriptors:
Target B2: Develop sustained positions, evaluate competing practical options and relay complex information with clear qualification.
4 — Fully achieves the specified purpose with precise relevant detail, coherent organisation and effective control at this target level.
3 — Achieves the main purpose; minor omissions or language lapses do not materially distort meaning.
2 — Partially achieves the purpose; important detail, organisation or language needs revision.
1 — Limited assessable evidence; major gaps or distortion impede the task.
0 — No assessable response or wholly unrelated response.
Rate each dimension separately. For mediation, invented facts, erased conditions or reversed agency prevent a high fidelity score. Do not penalise an accent or a defensible alternative phrasing. Scores describe this task only, not certified CEFR attainment.

retrieval.prompt: Without notes: recall 2 target expressions from Complex Listening & Inference; explain one source detail and use probably / assuming in a new example. Check meaning after attempting recall.
Without notes: recall 3 target expressions from Complex Listening & Inference; explain one source detail and use understatement in a new example. Check meaning after attempting recall.
Without notes: recall 4 target expressions from Complex Listening & Inference; explain one source detail and use not … but … in a new example. Check meaning after attempting recall.
Without notes: recall 5 target expressions from Complex Listening & Inference; explain one source detail and use probably / assuming in a new example. Check meaning after attempting recall.

remediation.action: Return to Readings A/B; underline the evidence for your statement, restore any lost condition, and say explicitly what remains unknown. Retry Q-B2-15-015 and the mediation task.
Revisit the three Lesson 2 models. Identify the intended function, correct the form, and produce a new example. Retrieve the missed expression again after one day.

masteryCheck.decision: Record evidence by construct; no pass mark or CEFR certification without human standard setting.
